note: The component library's role vocabulary. This file is the contract between the component layer (components/um-components.css, which may only read these variables) and the skin layer (themes/<id>.css, which must define every role). A role is either copied from a mood token (`from`) or computed from other roles (`derive`).

derivation.soft: mix(base, bg-page, w) — the brand colour blended toward the page background, so it recedes instead of competing. On a light theme this is a pale tint; on a dark theme it is a deep, desaturated version of the same hue. One formula, 32 themes.
derivation.strong: mix(base, text-primary, 0.2) — the brand colour moved toward the text colour. On a light theme that darkens it (a hover state); on a dark theme it brightens it. Element Plus writes `light-N`/`dark-N` because it only has one light theme plus a hand-written dark file; mixing toward white is wrong on a dark page, so this vocabulary names the direction instead.
derivation.why-not-element-names: `--el-color-primary-light-3` means "mixed with white", which is only correct on a light page. Naming by direction keeps one formula correct across all 32 moods. See docs/component-library.md for the correspondence table.

color-primary.doc: Brand / accent colour. Buttons, selected rows, active nav.

color-primary-on.doc: Readable foreground on a solid primary fill. Measured to reach 4.5:1.

color-primary-soft-8.doc: Primary, 80% toward the page background — a barely-there tint for selected rows.

color-primary-on-soft.doc: The foreground for a soft (tinted) surface: the brand colour moved toward the text colour just far enough to read on its own tint.

color-primary-strong.doc: The brand colour moved toward the text colour as far as its own on-colour stays readable against it. This is the hover state of a solid surface, so it may change visibly but never lose legibility.

color-success-on.doc: Readable foreground on a solid success fill.

color-success-on-soft.doc: The foreground for a soft (tinted) surface: the brand colour moved toward the text colour just far enough to read on its own tint.

color-success-strong.doc: The brand colour moved toward the text colour as far as its own on-colour stays readable against it. This is the hover state of a solid surface, so it may change visibly but never lose legibility.

color-warning-on.doc: Readable foreground on a solid warning fill.

color-warning-on-soft.doc: The foreground for a soft (tinted) surface: the brand colour moved toward the text colour just far enough to read on its own tint.

color-warning-strong.doc: The brand colour moved toward the text colour as far as its own on-colour stays readable against it. This is the hover state of a solid surface, so it may change visibly but never lose legibility.

color-danger-on.doc: Readable foreground on a solid danger fill.

color-danger-on-soft.doc: The foreground for a soft (tinted) surface: the brand colour moved toward the text colour just far enough to read on its own tint.

color-danger-strong.doc: The brand colour moved toward the text colour as far as its own on-colour stays readable against it. This is the hover state of a solid surface, so it may change visibly but never lose legibility.

color-info-on.doc: Readable foreground on a solid info fill — derived by the same rule as the state foregrounds.

color-info-on-soft.doc: The foreground for a soft (tinted) surface: the brand colour moved toward the text colour just far enough to read on its own tint.

color-info-strong.doc: The brand colour moved toward the text colour as far as its own on-colour stays readable against it. This is the hover state of a solid surface, so it may change visibly but never lose legibility.

text-secondary.doc: Supporting text. The mood owns a muted colour chosen for looks, and it is often below 4.5:1 as text. The library does not change the mood; it moves this role toward the text colour just far enough to read. It is measured against all three surfaces it can land on — the page, a floating overlay, and a container — because a caption that reads on the page can still vanish inside a card.

text-placeholder.doc: Placeholder text. The muted colour faded toward the surface it sits on — the input's own fill, not the page — as far as 2.5:1 allows. The bar is 2.5 rather than 4.5 because a placeholder is a hint, not content: WCAG treats it as exempt when the field carries a visible label, and Element Plus ships a comparable ~2:1. The surface it fades toward is the flattened one: a translucent fill over a translucent container is a colour that neither token names. If the muted colour does not even clear 2.5 on that surface, fading is not the answer and the role moves away from the surface instead — a placeholder that cannot be seen is not a placeholder. It is measured against every surface the component layer paints it on, not just the input's: the empty state's glyph sits on the light fill, and a role that is only guaranteed on the input can still vanish on that fill in four of the moods.

text-disabled.doc: Text of a disabled control. Faded toward the surface it sits on; deliberately faint, but still visible. A disabled button sits on the control fill while a disabled switch label sits on the page, so the role is faded against both — faded against only one of them, the other surface gets a label that is either invisible or not faded at all.

surface-control.doc: The effective surface of a control inside a container, flattened to one opaque colour. A translucent fill over a translucent container is a colour that neither token describes on its own, and text sitting on both is sitting on something neither of them names. Measured against the fill alone, the real surface is understated — in the frosted themes it puts a disabled label at 1.56:1.

surface-input.doc: The effective surface of a text field inside a container, flattened to one opaque colour. See surface-control.

surface-panel.doc: The effective surface of a panel cell, flattened to one opaque colour. It carries the same colour as the plain fill over the page, but it is a different job: this one is painted rather than only measured. A cell that sits on a line — a bordered table of key and value, where the gap between the cells *is* the line — cannot paint a translucent fill, because the line colour would come through it and lift the cell off the surface the contract describes. Painting the flattened colour gives the cell the colour it would have had anyway, in one layer, and the line stays in the gap.

surface-table-header.doc: The effective surface of a table's header cell: the recessed fill over the table's own fill, flattened to one opaque colour. A table paints its surface once, but the header paints a fill of its own on top of it, and a header measured against the fill alone is measured against a colour nobody sees.

fill-base.doc: A recessed surface sitting on the page.

fill-blank.doc: The plain surface a control sits on.

bg-container.doc: A container raised above the page.

bg-overlay.doc: A floating overlay: dropdown, dialog, drawer.

shadow-light.doc: Card elevation with its alpha halved. A shadow is not a colour, so it is weakened rather than mixed.

shadow-lighter.doc: Card elevation with its alpha quartered.

glow.doc: Quality hook: the mood's glow, applied to emphasis surfaces. Moods without one declare none.

backdrop.doc: Quality hook: the mood's backdrop filter for frosted surfaces.

color-primary-text.doc: The brand colour used as text — a text button, a link. Moved toward the text colour just far enough to read. It has to read on the page, on a floating overlay and inside a container5 on the overlay in four themes. The brutal accent is a bright yellow on a light page: readable as a fill, unreadable as text.

color-success-text.doc: The success colour used as text. Derived against the page, the overlay and the container together

color-warning-text.doc: The warning colour used as text. Derived against the page, the overlay and the container together

color-danger-text.doc: The danger colour used as text. Derived against the page, the overlay and the container together

color-info-text.doc: The info colour used as text. Derived against the page, the overlay and the container together

color-primary-graphic.doc: The brand colour used as a shape rather than as a fill — a timeline node, a checked box, a rating star. WCAG asks 3:1 of a graphic that has to be seen to be understood, not the 4.5:1 it asks of text, so the brand colour is moved just far enough to read as a shape. The raw colour is not enough: the brutal accent on a light container sits at 1.43:1, which is a checked checkbox nobody can see.

color-success-graphic.doc: The success colour used as a shape — a timeline node, a finished step.

color-warning-graphic.doc: The warning colour used as a shape — a timeline node, a rate's warning stars.

color-danger-graphic.doc: The danger colour used as a shape — a timeline node, an errored step.

color-info-graphic.doc: The info colour used as a shape.

shape-muted.doc: A shape that is only a placeholder and still has to be seen — the empty star of a rating, the empty box of a checkbox. The border roles are lines: a hairline is allowed to be faint, because the label beside it carries the meaning. A shape has no label. The empty star of a five-star rating is the scale: without it the three filled stars are just three shapes, and the reader cannot tell whether they are looking at a five-star rating or a three-star one. It is faded from the muted text colour — the faintest colour that still clears 3:1 — rather than from the border colour, because a mood may declare its border transparent (clay does), and a shape cannot be transparent and still be a shape.

optionalAbsentNote: The value an optional role takes when the mood does not declare it. It is written into the theme file all the same, because a role that is simply missing from a declaration list is a role that inherits from whichever theme file was linked after it — a mood with no glow would end up wearing another mood's glow.
componentConstantsNote: Shape and layout constants that are not theme parameters. A theme changes colours and metrics, not the fact that a circle is round. The component layer declares all of them; `validate` checks that it does and that it reads nothing else.

componentConstants.--um-radius-circle: 50% — a circle is round in every mood.
componentConstants.--um-radius-none: 0 — for moods that want a hard edge.
componentConstants.--um-focus-ring-offset: Gap between a focused control and its ring.
componentConstants.--um-space-md: Derived spacing step between the theme's small and extra-small.
componentConstants.--um-space-xl: Derived spacing step above the theme's section gap.
componentConstants.--um-height-sm: Control height for the small size, derived from the theme's type size.
componentConstants.--um-height-md: Control height for the default size.
componentConstants.--um-height-lg: Control height for the large size.
componentConstants.--um-mirror: 1, or -1 in a right-to-left reader: a shape that points along the reading direction turns over.
